title: Positive-degree part of injective Cech augmentation
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], U_i an arbitrary open cover of X, and J an injective sheaf of O_X-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Let C(U,J) be the Cech cochain complex of the presheaf of global-section-ring modules [def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex]. Global sections are the evaluation functor of [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology]. Let b be a cochain map from the single-term complex J(X)[0] to C(U,J), whose degree-zero component is the canonical restriction map into the product over Fin 1-tuples, preceded by the identity restriction-of-scalars identification at X. The structure-sheaf map from X to itself is identified with the identity ring homomorphism, by a supplied proof ht of that equality. Then the homology map of b in every degree n > 0 is an isomorphism. This concerns one injective module, with no injective resolution or total complex.

source.place: Tag 01EP (lemma-injective-trivial-cech), degree-zero and positive-degree clauses, as used in the augmented-row argument of Tag 01EQ (lemma-cech-cohomology).

proof.text: Write n = q + 1. Apply the proved source-library theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.isFlasque_of_injective to J and TopCat.Sheaf.exactAt_cechComplex_of_isFlasque to its underlying abelian sheaf. This gives zero homology at q + 1 in the explicit intersection complex. These are existing fully proved tools, also used by the former acyclicity dependency; no new open vanishing theorem is introduced.

Transport this zero object along the proved TopCat.Presheaf.cechComplexFunctorHomologyIso U J.presheafModuleCat (q + 1). Its source is the abelian group underlying the homology of Mathlib cechComplexFunctor. The forgetful functor reflects subsingletonness, so ModuleCat.isZero_iff_subsingleton gives zero homology of the target complex.

HomologicalComplex.isZero_single_obj_homology gives zero homology of the single-term source because n is positive. IsZero.isIso shows the homology map of b is an isomorphism; quasiIsoAt_iff_isIso_homologyMap finishes. The covering and augmentation-component hypotheses are not needed in positive degree.

proof_origin.place: Tag 01EP; the source-library flasque route for positive degree, and sheaf gluing in degree zero. T2 second reading, 2026-10-12.

from.place: Strict degree part of the augmented Cech quasi-isomorphism

lean.statement:
theorem injectiveModuleCechAugmentation_quasiIsoAt_positive {X : Scheme.{u}} {ι : Type u}
    (U : ι → X.Opens) (_hU : iSup U = ⊤) (J : X.Modules) [Injective J]
    (ht : (X.ringCatSheaf.obj.map (isTerminalTop.op.to (op ⊤))).hom =
      RingHom.id Γ(X, ⊤))
    (b : (CochainComplex.single₀ (ModuleCat.{u} Γ(X, ⊤))).obj
        ((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).obj J) ⟶
      (CategoryTheory.cechComplexFunctor U).obj J.presheafModuleCat)
    (_hb : b.f 0 =
      (ModuleCat.restrictScalarsId'App
        (X.ringCatSheaf.obj.map (isTerminalTop.op.to (op ⊤))).hom ht
        (J.val.obj (op ⊤))).inv ≫
      Pi.lift fun y : Fin 1 → ι =>
        J.presheafModuleCat.map (homOfLE (le_top (a := ∏ᶜ fun l => U (y l)))).op)
    (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) : QuasiIsoAt b n
